text:
Maria R.: Postmortem follow-up kickoff for INF-2389 (KV cache OOM sequence). goal: clear owners, short-term mitigations, and a 3-week verification cadence. I sketched a risk/priority matrix in the PM doc. pls volunteer or object.
Alex T.: I can own the profiling + nightly snapshots. will instrument allocator metrics (jemalloc/tcmalloc) and push dashboards.
Jamal S.: I'll run GC/compaction experiments and try a small off-heap cache prototype.
Ingrid L.: Ops will own alerts, canary gating, and the emergency rollback playbook. Also propose a soft-memory watermark at 65% host mem for SEV3 and 80% for SEV2.
Patrick H.: Devex will add the remediation checklist, impact table, and a sample cost projection for TTL changes.
sre-bot: Incident INF-2389 archived as RESOLVED; follow-ups required.
Maria R.: Suggested split: 1) Leak triage & repro (Alex), 2) Runtime mitigations + GC (Jamal), 3) Operational controls (Ingrid + SRE). Deliverables: EOW snapshot + week 2 experiment results + week 3 RCA verification.
Alex T.: Quick note from heap diffs: retained-bytes in shard index grow ~30MB per heavy insert burst. snippet from `mallinfo` export:
```
arena: 120 MB, uordblks: 910M, fordblks: 20M, retained: 320M
```
Pattern: bursts with many small writes then seconds of inactivity -> fragmentation increases.
Jamal S.: Repro PR in draft: small harness that feeds 100k small keys with interleaved large-seq reads. initial run shows fragmentation spike. opening INF-2401 for the repro + instrumentation.
Ingrid L.: Alert proposal: add metric `kv_cache_rss_ratio` aggregated per-host and cluster. rule: if 3 hosts in a zone exceed 0.78 for 5 minutes -> SEV2. also auto-collect `pmap`, `/proc/<pid>/smaps`, and upload to debug bucket.
Maria R.: Can we avoid bounce during debug? prefer heap dump + remote analysis first.
Ingrid L.: yes, dump + S3 upload by default. only reboot as last resort.
Patrick H.: Cost note: lowering TTL reduces cache hit rate; I estimated +12% request cost at -50% TTL. will attach a table in INF-2402.
Alex T.: Short mitigation idea: shard-local eviction on memory pressure. can be a node-local signal to reduce growth. low-risk; I'll prototype.
Jamal S.: For GC: try the following in week 2: aggressive background purging every 10m, and enable `MALLOC_TRIM_THRESHOLD` tuning. rollback criteria: if request latency regress > 5% or fragmentation not improved.
ci-bot: New CI job queued: mem-pressure-smoke (5m).
Alex T.: CI regression: agree to add a small mem-pressure job that runs on PRs touching runtime or cache. ci-bot, please make it non-blocking for now, blocking after week 3 if stable.
ci-bot: job will run as non-blocking for 3 weeks then auto-promote to blocking if no failures.
Ingrid L.: Canary gating rule: compare canary memory slope vs control. if slope > control * 1.15 over 4h -> pause rollout and page oncall.
Maria R.: Ownership recap + tickets: Alex -> INF-2401 (profiling + snapshots + eviction prototype), Jamal -> INF-2403 (GC trials + off-heap prototype), Ingrid -> INF-2404 (alerts, runbook, canary gates), Patrick -> INF-2402 (cost analysis + docs). I'll add target dates.
Alex T.: Permission note: need read access to jemalloc metrics in prod. Ingrid, can you grant `alex-team:metrics:read` for 14 days?
Ingrid L.: Granted for 14 days. :white_check_mark:
Jamal S.: I'll also try a lightweight background recycler thread in the runtime to batch frees; if it reduces fragmentation by >10% in 24h, we can promote.
Patrick H.: I'll prep a short slide for weekly WG summarizing customer impact and expected TTBR (time to bottom-line reduction).
Maria R.: Weekly cadence: 30m triage every Friday 09:30 for next 3 weeks. first meeting this Friday. please add docs to the PM page and create PRs for runbook edits.
Alex T.: Posting first-nightly heap dumps to INF-2401 now.
Jamal S.: :thumbsup: repro PR posted, link in ticket.
Patrick H.: scheduling invites for Fridays.
Maria R.: thanks all — I'll mark this thread with follow-ups and close once the first Friday meeting happens.
